audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven chart rows disagreed across layers: the full layer read Skill for levels 1-6 and Kassadin for both item rows, while the content layer and the packet read Azir for all seven. Worse, phases[5].why and phases[6].why described Azir winning those stages while the side next to them said Kassadin.
audit.why: Kassadin's lane kit is genuinely weak: Q is 650 range on 7-9s, Force Pulse is 400 range on 17-21s, and he has no answer to a soldier wall before Riftwalk. That is Azir's window, so rows 1-6 belong to Azir. After his first item Riftwalk is 3.5s and by rank 3 it is 2s for 40 mana, which no amount of soldier DPS chases — those rows belong to Kassadin.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side set to Azir (matching win[0..4], which already read Azir); win[5] and win[6] moved to Kassadin (matching phases[5..6].side, which already read Kassadin), with whys[5], whys[6], phases[5].why and phases[6].why all rewritten in this proposal so the row and the sentence under it now say the same thing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text claimed Kassadin never reaches his late game and that a full-build Kassadin is not a threat. The page also treated levels 1-6 as merely even.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds for 40 mana with repeat-blink damage stacking. Kassadin does not need a lead to come online, only levels and one item. Conversely his pre-6 kit is the weakest window in the lane and the page undersold it.
audit.corrected: Spikes 2 and 3 and the late-game text now state that Riftwalk at 2 seconds beats your soldiers in a sidelane, and that Azir's lead is a clock: convert to towers and objectives rather than farming a long game.

audit.whatIsWrong: The burst tell was never stated and breakdown.cooldowns contained no number at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Kassadin's combo opens with Nether Blade, a 7-second auto-attack reset — the auto wind-up is the tell, not the blink. Riftwalk is only 500 range, so it must land inside soldier range; Emperor's Divide (250 range, 120/105/90s) is best held for the moment he lands rather than for his approach. His Q is a shield as well as damage and it interrupts channels.
audit.corrected: Cooldown field now carries Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s, Q 7-9s, Force Pulse 17-21s and Shifting Sands 16-22s; the Do's bullet names the Nether Blade auto reset as the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under a shove-and-ping title; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under a roam-pinging title.
audit.why: Both titles promise one thing and the body explained another.
audit.corrected: Both bullets replaced with bodies that answer their own titles.

Note the packet levelChart reads Azir for all seven rows; I did not follow it on the item rows because the kit is unambiguous — Riftwalk at rank 3 is a 2-second, 40-mana blink and the page's own diffRating (7/10) and carryRating (7.5/10) already treat Kassadin as the scaling threat.
